chunk_findings.detail: The overdue-cadence blockers are appended to `v.blockers` *after* the validation verdict `v.may_complete` has already been produced, and the success/failure decision is then taken from that precomputed value rather than from the (now mutated) blocker list. Concretely: run `ddflow complete <phase>` on a phase whose only outstanding issue is a due `architecture_review`. The new loop appends the "periodic pass overdue: architecture_review …" string to `v.blockers`, but `v.may_complete` is a value carried on the validation result, so it is still `True`; the guard `if not v.may_complete and not force` therefore does not fire, and the command takes the success path. The phase closes even though the report it returns contains the overdue blocker (the dict's `"blockers"` entry aliases the same list), which is exactly the case the change is supposed to refuse ("completing a phase with a due architecture_review is refused"). Mutation of the blocker list alone cannot flip a boolean that was computed before the mutation; either `may_complete` must be recomputed/derived from `blockers` at this point, or the cadence check must be run before the verdict is built.

chunk_findings.detail: The extracted helper re-runs config parsing itself: `calendar = _calendar(cfg) if calendar is None else calendar`. The `try/except ValueError` that used to wrap `_calendar(cfg)` stayed behind in `cadence`, so the helper is only safe when the caller happens to pass a pre-validated `calendar`. The whole reason the helper was introduced is the new `complete <phase>` path, and a natural call there is `due_cadences(repo, cfg, st)` relying on the documented default — on a repo whose cadence calendar is malformed (the same input for which `cadence()` cleanly returns `O.failed("cadence", str(exc), due=[])` at operations.py:150-153), `_calendar` raises `ValueError` out of `due_cadences`, so `complete` crashes with a traceback instead of refusing/reporting. The two callers of the same shared routine now disagree on how a bad calendar surfaces.

chunk_findings.detail: The old `cadence` wrapped `_calendar(cfg)` in `try/except ValueError` and converted a bad cadence-interval config into `O.failed("cadence", str(exc), due=[])`. The new shared function drops that guard: when it is called without a precomputed calendar — which is exactly the advertised call site, `complete <phase>` (`due_cadences(repo, cfg, st)` with the default `calendar=None`) — a malformed interval in the cadence config makes `_calendar(cfg)` raise `ValueError` straight out of `due_cadences`. Concretely, with a config whose calendar interval is unparseable, `cadence` reports a structured failure while `complete <phase>` (which previously never touched cadence and therefore always worked) now dies with an uncaught `ValueError` from this line, unless the caller in the not-shown part independently reproduces the same `try/except`. The guard should have moved into `due_cadences` rather than being left only in the `cadence` wrapper.

chunk_findings.detail:
The diff deletes the only code that turned an overdue phase-scoped cadence into a hard stop for `complete <phase>`:

- it removed the `if it.kind == "phase": ... from .operations import due_cadences` block that filtered `d["unit"] == "phases"` and appended `"periodic pass overdue: ..."` to `v.blockers`.
- nothing in the remaining part of this diff re-adds that enforcement. `ddflow/api/operations.py` `due_cadences` is now purely a data provider (`count_due(...) + lessons_cadence(...) + export_cadence(...) + _calendar_due(...)`); it returns dicts and never touches `v.blockers`/`v.may_complete`. The removal is therefore not compensated anywhere in the code under review.

Concrete failure: with `cfg.cadence.architecture_review_every_phases = 1`, one phase already `done`, and no `architecture_review` entry in `st.cadences`, the old code appended a blocker and `if not v.may_complete and not force:` returned `O.refused(...)`. After this diff that block is gone, so `ddflow complete <phase>` returns success — exactly the case the change's own acceptance test says must be refused ("completing a phase with a due architecture_review is refused, and passes after `cadence --ran`"). Either the enforcement was accidentally dropped from this hunk, or the refactor into `count_due`/`due_cadences` changed the wrong layer and `complete` no longer consults cadences at all.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle.py (complete() phase handling, hunk at ~line 1412)

chunk_findings.detail: `phase_overdue` builds its skip set purely from the *names* on the left of each `every_days` spec (`{spec.partition("=")[0].strip() ...}`), and `count_due` then unconditionally `continue`s past any name in `replaced`. Because the day value is deliberately never validated ("read leniently"), a same-name malformed entry removes the count-based gate while the calendar machinery cannot fire either. Concretely, with `every_days = ["architecture_review=1O"]` (digit-1/letter-O typo, or `architecture_review=oops`) and `architecture_review_every_phases = 1` with a phase already done, `replaced == {"architecture_review"}`, so the loop hits `if name in replaced: continue` and `phase_overdue` returns no blocker for `architecture_review`; `ddflow complete <phase>` is accepted with an overdue architecture review. This directly contradicts the function's own docstring ("a typo elsewhere in `every_days` cannot switch this check off") for the case that matters — a typo in the pass's own entry — and the accompanying regression test only exercises an unrelated name (`bug_hunt=oops`), so it cannot catch it.

chunk_findings.detail: This hunk deletes the only place where `complete <phase>` refuses an overdue phase-scoped cadence, and replaces it with nothing. The removed code called `due_cadences(...)`, filtered `d["unit"] == "phases"`, and appended each overdue pass to `v.blockers`, which feeds `v.may_complete`; without it the result dict's `"blockers"` no longer contains the overdue pass, so `may_complete` stays true. Concretely: given a repo with `cadence.architecture_review_every_phases = 1`, a done phase, and no `architecture_review` run since, the old code returned a blocker ("periodic pass overdue: architecture_review ...") and `not v.may_complete and not force` returned `O.refused("item.completed", ...)`; after this change the same input completes the phase successfully. That is exactly the scenario the stated test asserts must be refused ("completing a phase with a due architecture_review is refused, and passes after cadence --ran"), and it also contradicts the stated goal (a) that `complete <phase>` list due cadences as unmet conditions — this diff removes that check rather than adding one. If a later part of the change is intended to reintroduce it via the gate/unmet-condition mechanism, that reintroduction is not present in the code under review, so as it stands the enforcement is gone.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle.py:1415 (removed `if it.kind == "phase":` cadence-blocker block in `complete`)

chunk_findings.detail: `replaced` is built purely by string-partitioning the *name* out of each `every_days` entry, with the value deliberately unvalidated ("no validation"). Because `count_due` then unconditionally `continue`s for any name in `replaced`, a *malformed* calendar entry whose name is the same as a phase-counted pass silently removes the only phase-close enforcement for that pass—and nothing else in the diff (the verdict gets only `phase_overdue`) replaces it. So the guard the change is built around is exactly the guard that can be switched off by a config typo. Concretely, with `architecture_review_every_phases = 1`, one completed phase, and `.ddflow/config.toml` containing `every_days = ["architecture_review=oops"]`, `replaced == {"architecture_review"}`, so `count_due` skips architecture_review and `phase_overdue` returns `[]` instead of refusing; `ddflow complete <phase>` is allowed even though architecture_review is overdue by the per-phase count. This contradicts the function's own stated contract ("so a typo elsewhere in `every_days` cannot switch this check off") and the intent that a phase cannot complete while a phase-scoped cadence is overdue. The test added alongside it (`test_a_malformed_calendar_knob_does_not_switch_the_check_off`) only uses the *unrelated* name `bug_hunt=oops`, so it passes without exercising this case; the same hole exists for a valid-but-overdue same-name entry (e.g. `architecture_review=1`), since `phase_overdue` never consults calendar due-ness. `replaced` should only suppress the count-based pass for entries whose value actually parses/enables the calendar pass.
